- If sentiment is positive (≥ 0.25) and forecast is rising sharply, reduce peak overshoot by 5–10% to avoid overreaction.
- If sentiment is negative (≤ -0.25) and forecast is falling, avoid premature bottoming — delay correction by 1–2 periods.
- When sentiment shows strong reversal (e.g., from +1 to -1), model should adjust downward by 3–5% in next 3–5 periods.
- If recent history shows mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days trending down), forecast should not continue upward unless sentiment confirms breakout.
- For 30-day horizon, if forecast exceeds true outcome by >10% in first 5–7 days, reduce subsequent days’ forecast by 2–3% to avoid momentum bias.
- If sentiment is neutral (0.00) and price is trending, model should not overfit to recent volatility — use 3–5 period moving average for smoothing.
- If forecast spikes after a sharp drop (e.g., 10%+ drop in 2 days), reduce spike magnitude by 15–20% to avoid false recovery signals.
- When sentiment is consistently 0.00 and price is flat, forecast should not deviate more than ±2% from recent 5-day average to avoid noise amplification.
